rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): suppress native browser context menu
rawCommits.body:
Right-clicking empty AURA chrome was showing the WebView2 / Chromium
native menu (Back, Refresh, Save as, Print, More tools, Inspect),
breaking the desktop OS feel. Install a single document-level listener
that defers to any in-app onContextMenu (DesktopContextMenu,
NotesEntryContextMenu, ProcessCanvas, ...) via event.defaultPrevented,
and otherwise cancels the native menu. Inside editable text fields
(input, textarea, contenteditable) we replace the native menu with a
compact in-app Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All so right-click editing
still works without giving up control of the chrome.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: suppress native browser context menu

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): widen top-edge resize hit area on Windows
rawCommits.body:
The borderless main window inherits tao's default WM_NCHITTEST
behavior, which only reports HTTOP within SM_CYFRAME (~4 logical
px) of the top edge. Combined with the floating titlebar pill
that begins 5 px below the window edge, hitting the resize zone
required pixel-perfect aim.

Install a Win32 subclass on the main HWND that returns
HTTOP/HTTOPLEFT/HTTOPRIGHT for any cursor inside a 10-logical-px
band along the top, falling through to DefSubclassProc for every
other position so titlebar drag, side resize, and Chromium
app-region all keep working unchanged. The subclass is dispatched
before tao's by virtue of being installed last, becomes a no-op
while the window is maximized, and re-reads DPI on each hit-test
so it stays consistent across mixed-DPI monitor setups.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: widen top-edge resize hit area on Windows

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): defer-open pattern for async-loading modals
rawCommits.body:
When the user clicked Delete on an agent attached to multiple
projects, the confirm modal opened immediately, then janked: the
"Delete" button widened to "Delete and remove from N projects" and
a cascade-warning paragraph appeared once bindings finished loading.
Same flicker existed for the marketplace Hire modal (in-modal
spinner -> project list) and the Tier subscription modal ("Loading
plan details..." -> tier grid).

Introduce useDeferredModalOpen, a tiny shared hook that runs the
caller's prepare() (e.g. cascade.refresh / projectsStore.refresh /
billingStore.fetchSubscription), keeps the modal closed and shows a
disabled trigger button until the prepare resolves, and only then
flips isOpen true. A 3000ms failsafe opens the modal even if prepare
never settles. Stale resolutions from a previous open cycle are
ignored via an internal cycle token.

Apply to three call sites:
- DeleteAgentConfirmModal (AgentList + AgentInfoPanel) - also shorten
  the cascade label from "Delete and remove from N projects" to
  "Delete (N projects)" so width is stable across binding counts.
- HireProjectPickerModal (MarketplaceMainPanel) - drop the in-modal
  spinner; the per-card Hire button disables briefly while preparing.
- TierSubscriptionModal (OrgSettingsPanel via OrgSettingsRewards /
  OrgSettingsBilling) - read subscription from billing-store instead
  of fetching on open; the Upgrade / Change Plan trigger disables
  briefly while preparing.

The remaining modals from the audit (AgentSelectorModal,
BuyCreditsModal, ProjectSettingsModal, etc.) are deliberately left
for follow-up PRs - the shared hook is the substrate for those.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: defer-open pattern for async-loading modals

rawCommits.subject: feat: split AURA into dev and stable build channels
rawCommits.body:
Introduce a build-time channel selector on aura-os-core
(`stable-channel` default, `dev-channel` opt-in via cargo features)
so a `cargo run`-built dev AURA can run side-by-side with the
installed stable AURA on one machine without colliding on data
dirs, ports, single-instance locks, skills trees, or window
identity. Remote services stay shared via .env.

The new `Channel` enum in `aura-os-core::channel` is the single
source of truth for every per-channel identifier: data dir name
(`aura` vs `aura-dev`), skills home (`~/.aura` vs `~/.aura-dev`),
Windows single-instance mutex, window/menu title, embedded
desktop server port (19847 vs 19848), standalone server port
(3100 vs 3101), harness sidecar port (19080 vs 19081), default
harness URL port (8080 vs 8081), and updater enablement (off in
dev so a cargo-built shell can never silently replace itself
with the stable installer).

`cargo run -p aura-os-desktop` and the `scripts/dev/*` runners
default to the dev channel via cargo's default feature. The
release pipeline (`cargo packager`, `verify-desktop.mjs`, the
`release-stable` and `release-nightly` workflows) builds with
`--no-default-features --features stable-channel`. The desktop
crate disables default features on its `aura-os-core` and
`aura-os-server` deps so a stable packaging build cannot
accidentally pull in `dev-channel` from a transitive default.

Dev script defaults bumped to dev-channel ports (Vite 5174,
mobile backend 3101) so a developer running `npm run dev` or the
mobile runner does not bind on top of an installed stable AURA.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: split AURA into dev and stable build channels

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): re-enable 3D chat mode with image-first flow
rawCommits.body:
Bring back the 3D pill in the chat mode selector and rewire it so
the only valid path is "generate an image first, then convert it to
3D" -- exactly how the standalone AURA 3D app works. Manual image
attachments for chat 3D mode are disabled because the proxy decode-
and-forward route is broken; the legacy code path is left in place
but commented out so flipping it back on is trivial once the proxy
is fixed.

The input bar now derives its 3D source from the most recent
successful generate_image tool result in the thread, surfaces it
as a "Source for 3D" thumbnail above the textarea, blocks Send with
a "switch to Image mode" hint until one exists, and dispatches the
3D request via generate3dStream's URL form. The resolved-send
pipeline carries sourceImageUrl through to both the live and
queue-replay paths.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: re-enable 3D chat mode with image-first flow

rawCommits.body:
The AURA 3D app's Image tab was the only call site appending the
product-photography STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX to user prompts. Send the prompt
verbatim instead so image generation behaves consistently with chat

rawCommits.subject: fix(agents): recognize renamed CEO via system-prompt prefix
rawCommits.body:
After renaming the bootstrap CEO (e.g. "CEO" -> "Maia") and re-logging
in, the server was creating a duplicate "CEO" agent. `looks_like_ceo`
only recognised renamed CEOs via the locally-stamped
`bootstrap:ceo_agent_id` setting or an exact name+role both equal to
"CEO". CEOs created before commit 2dabef61a (the stamping fix) never
had the local stamp, so a post-rename login fell through both checks
and `dedupe_ceo_agents` returned no canonical, causing
`setup_ceo_agent` to mint a fresh duplicate.

Add a third identity signal: the canonical CEO `system_prompt` prefix
("You are the CEO SuperAgent"), extracted into a shared constant so
the matcher and the template stay in lock-step. The agent editor
preserves `system_prompt` on save unless the user explicitly rewrites
it, so this prefix survives a rename and lets the dedupe step pick the
older renamed CEO as canonical and best-effort delete the freshly-
minted duplicate on the next setup call.

Adds four unit tests: renamed-name-only, full rename, arbitrary system
prompt is not a CEO, and a drift guard that `ceo_system_prompt()`
always starts with `CEO_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: recognize renamed CEO via system-prompt prefix

agentDisplayName helper that yields "New Agent" for null/undefined or

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): suppress focus-visible outline on dialog/modal wrappers
rawCommits.body:
Container elements with `tabindex="-1"`, `role="dialog"`, or
`aria-modal="true"` are focused programmatically for keyboard /
screen-reader scope management, not as tab stops. When the user pressed
Shift (or Shift+Tab) Chromium flipped into keyboard-modality, and the
zui Modal's `modalRef.current?.focus()` call on its `tabIndex={-1}`
wrapper triggered the global `:focus-visible` rule and painted a 2px
white ring around the entire modal box. Extend the existing
`#root` / `.titlebar-drag` opt-out to also cover those container
patterns (and both `:focus` and `:focus-visible` for keyboard-modality
edge cases) so high-level wrappers never paint a focus ring while real
interactive controls keep their accessible focus indicator.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rendered.title: Native-feeling chrome, a reborn 3D chat flow, and side-by-side dev builds
rendered.intro: Today's nightly reshapes how AURA feels as a desktop app — right-click menus, resize edges, and modal openings all behave more like native chrome — while chat picks up a proper image-to-3D pipeline, clickable session history, and a "+" for starting a fresh conversation. Under the hood, dev and stable builds can now coexist on the same machine without stepping on each other.

entries.title: In-app context menu replaces the WebView2 native menu
entries.summary: Right-clicking AURA chrome no longer leaks the Chromium Back/Refresh/Inspect menu; editable fields get a tailored Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All instead.

items.text: A document-level handler suppresses the native WebView2/Chromium context menu across AURA chrome while still deferring to in-app menus (DesktopContextMenu, NotesEntryContextMenu, ProcessCanvas) that call preventDefault.

Inside inputs, textareas, and contenteditable regions, right-click now opens a compact in-app Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All menu so editing keyboards still work without giving up control of the chrome.

entries.title: Easier top-edge window resize on Windows
entries.summary: The borderless main window now exposes a generous resize band along the top edge so dragging to resize no longer requires pixel-perfect aim.

items.text: A Win32 subclass on the main HWND reports HTTOP/HTTOPLEFT/HTTOPRIGHT for any cursor inside a 10-logical-px band along the top edge, replacing tao's default ~4px frame and fixing the conflict with the floating titlebar pill.

The hit-test becomes a no-op while maximized, re-reads DPI on every call for mixed-DPI setups, and falls through to DefSubclassProc so titlebar drag, side resize, and Chromium app-region behavior are unchanged.

entries.title: Modals open at their final size instead of jumping
entries.summary: A new shared hook holds modals closed until their async data is ready, eliminating the flicker on agent delete, marketplace hire, and tier upgrade.

items.text: Introduced useDeferredModalOpen, which runs a prepare() step (cascade refresh, projects refresh, billing fetch), keeps the trigger disabled until it resolves, and only then opens the modal — with a 3000ms failsafe and stale-cycle guard.

Applied to DeleteAgentConfirmModal, HireProjectPickerModal, and TierSubscriptionModal so each opens once at its final width with stable copy; the cascade button label was also shortened to 'Delete (N projects)' so width no longer depends on binding count.

entries.title: Dev and stable AURA can now coexist on one machine
entries.summary: A build-time channel selector gives dev builds their own data dir, ports, single-instance lock, and disabled updater so a cargo-run AURA never collides with the installed stable app.

items.text: Added a Channel enum in aura-os-core as the single source of truth for per-channel identity: data dir (aura vs aura-dev), skills home, Windows mutex, window/menu title, embedded server port (19847/19848), standalone server port (3100/3101), harness sidecar port (19080/19081), and default harness URL port (8080/8081).

The updater is compiled out in dev so a cargo-built shell can never silently replace itself with the stable installer, and the desktop crate disables default features on its core/server deps so stable packaging can't transitively pull in dev-channel.

CI release workflows (desktop-validate, release-nightly, release-stable) and dev runner scripts were rewired so packaged builds use stable-channel while npm run dev / cargo run default to dev-channel on isolated ports (Vite 5174, mobile backend 3101).

entries.title: 3D chat mode returns with an image-first pipeline
entries.summary: The 3D pill is back in the chat mode selector, wired to derive its source image from the latest in-thread generation, and AURA 3D's image tab stops silently style-locking prompts.

items.text: Re-enabled the 3D mode pill and rewired chat so 3D requests pull their source from the most recent successful generate_image tool result, surfaced as a 'Source for 3D' thumbnail above the textarea; the resolved-send pipeline carries sourceImageUrl through both live and queue-replay paths.

Stopped appending the product-photography STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX to user prompts in the AURA 3D app's Image tab so image generation behaves consistently with chat /image and /3d; stripStyleLock still cleans the suffix off legacy artifacts.

entries.title: Chat 3D pipeline, clickable sessions, and a wave of UI polish
entries.summary: A long evening of interface work: chat 3D became a true two-step in-bar pipeline with an inline GLB viewer, chat sessions got titles and click-to-open, feedback gained a Details/Comments split, plus dozens of smaller fixes across context menus, theming, and release tooling.

items.text: Reworked chat 3D as an in-bar two-step image→model pipeline with a removable pinned source thumb owned by chat-ui-store, then moved that thumb inline into the input row, allowed image-only sends to dispatch the model step, and replaced Model3DBlock's download link with an embedded lazy-loaded WebGLViewer plus auto-expand for generated 3D blocks.

Agent Chats sidekick now auto-summarizes session titles via Haiku regardless of token-count gating, hides truly untitled rows, and rows are clickable — opening the historical transcript while staying inside the current app shell (agents stays in agents). A new '+' button on the chat input mode row starts a fresh session, scoped via a live-session store so the visible transcript belongs to the current SessionReady.

Extended the new in-app context menu with a Copy entry for non-editable text selections in chat/markdown output and an image branch with Copy Image (re-encoding non-PNG sources to PNG via canvas, with a CORS fallback) so right-click works everywhere it should.

Feedback got a Notes-style sidekick split into Details and Comments tabs (driven by a sidekickTab slice on the feedback store), and every new submission is now tagged with the active app version — surfaced in the modal and as a vX.Y.Z chip on each feed card — via the existing metadata blob with no schema changes.

Theming and chrome polish: a new --color-modal-bg token gives modals a jet-black background in dark mode (with a paired Dark+Light editor in Settings → Appearance), the zui Button dim now sits at full opacity at rest and dims on hover, the titlebar Update pill renders at full accent saturation, and dialog wrappers no longer paint a stray focus ring on Shift/Tab.

Chat reading and composing improvements: explicit upward scroll intent now overrides streaming auto-follow and the post-stream image pin so the user's reading position holds, the empty-state suggestion chips were redesigned as a 2x2 segmented grid with a slower 6s input pulse, the bottom-bar environment slot stays width-stable while agent metadata loads, image attachments get breathing room, and the MODE row no longer text-selects on drag.

Project settings can now attach an Orbit repo from the edit modal (reusing OrbitRepoSection from the new-project flow) with the server's update_project handler calling orbit.ensure_repo when a brand-new owner+repo is supplied, and sidebar agent rows fall back to a 'New Agent' label so blank-named agents still have a recognizable identifier.

Server-side, renamed CEO agents (e.g. 'CEO' → 'Maia') are now recognized via a canonical system_prompt prefix so post-rename logins no longer mint duplicate 'CEO' agents that the dedupe step couldn't reconcile.

Release pipeline fix: cargo packager 0.11.8 doesn't accept --no-default-features/--features, which was breaking CI; those flags are now applied via before-packaging-command in the desktop crate's Cargo.toml so packaged builds still pin to stable-channel.

highlights: Native browser context menu replaced with in-app menus across editable, text, and image targets
Chat 3D mode reborn as a two-step image→model flow with an embedded GLB viewer
Dev and stable AURA builds run side-by-side with isolated data dirs and ports
Windows top-edge resize is finally easy to grab
Agent chat sessions are now clickable, auto-titled, and a '+' starts a fresh chat
